_about: How well Tip of the Tongue works in each language, measured on 2026-10-26. Picture sets were built from a 20-word list per language (the English demo list, translated); spoken naming was checked with speech synthesized by macOS voices, never recordings of people. Method and caveats: docs/languages.md.

table.recommended_form: the bare word (the article didn't help)
a frame (यह बिल्ली है) was tried and didn't help; use the bare word
with a measure word (一只猫, 一把剪刀)

status_levels.verified: Picture set and Muse Spark naming at least 19/20, spoken naming at least 18/20 in the recommended answer form with two voices or runs, and the scoring rules for the language tested. Codes still get a person's review, as in every language.
status_levels.works with review: Pictures and naming work and spoken naming is mostly right in the recommended form, but known gaps mean a person should check every code that isn't Correct.
status_levels.experimental: Measured below that, or not measured. Usable for building pictures; don't rely on automatic spoken scoring.

method.picture_sets: scripts/build_test_set.py, line style, 2 candidates per word: Muse Spark plans each picture, Muse Image draws, SAM 3.1 checks for one clear object, Muse Spark names the picture in the test language and naming_errors.classify scores that name. kept = at least one candidate passed both checks. First-pass numbers, before reviewer edits.
method.named_by_muse_spark: Words for which Muse Spark's one-word name for at least one candidate picture was coded Correct.
method.spoken: Each of the 20 words synthesized on its own with macOS `say`, converted to 16 kHz mono WAV, padded with 0.7 s of silence, transcribed by Muse Voice Transcribe with the language hint and coded by naming_errors.classify with the set's accepted alternates, as the Scorer does. correct = transcripts coded Correct. One run of 20 per entry; expect a few points of run-to-run variation.

untested_languages: Any other language: Test Studio will try (Muse Spark and Muse Image take any language) and Muse Voice Transcribe accepts a hint for 25 languages, but nothing is measured, so the status is experimental.

languages.name: English
languages.summary: Reference language: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary and WordNet rules.

recommended.answer_form: the bare word (the article didn't help)

notes: Daniel (en-GB) heard three short or borrowed words as other words: saw -> 'So', harp -> 'huh', igloo -> 'Hey, Blue'.
Samantha wrote 'umbrellaumbrella'. The Scorer now reads a name that was written twice as one word.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.summary: Verified when people name with the article. Bare words depend on the voice: 13/20 with a Spain voice, 18/20 with a Mexican one.
notes: Picture set: Muse Spark called the sierra (saw) pictures 'serrucho' (hand saw); the item went to review.
Bare words from Mónica (es-ES) became spelling variants or near-misses: Kuchara, Cierra, Paraguás, Acla, Baco, Janahoria, Arba.

Counting exact homophones as Correct, as French and Portuguese now do, would make it 15/20 (Mónica) and 20/20 (Paulina). It's not applied, because the brief keeps Spanish scoring unchanged; it's a one-line change (HOMOPHONE_LANGS) for the lead to approve.

languages.name: French
languages.summary: Verified when people name with the article (19/20 and 20/20). Bare one-syllable words are often heard as other words (banc -> 'Dans').
notes: Scoring rules: articles, elision (l'ancre), plurals, rough spelling-to-sound rules, and homophones counted as Correct (une encre -> ancre).
Muse Spark named one of the kettle pictures 'théière' (teapot); the other picture was kept.
Flagged meanings: banc (sandbank, shoal) and bougie (spark plug).
Amélie (fr-CA) got 15/20 on bare words and 20/20 with the article.

languages.name: Brazilian Portuguese
languages.summary: Verified for Brazilian Portuguese when people name with the article (19/20 and 18/20, one Brazilian voice, two runs).
notes: Only one Brazilian macOS voice (Luciana). A European Portuguese voice (Joana) saying the Brazilian words got 14/20 bare and 16/20 with the article.
guarda-chuva is the hardest word: 'Guarda a chuva' and 'Quando ar da chuva'. Hyphenated targets match with or without the hyphen.
Homophone spellings count as Correct (cerrote -> serrote, Senoura -> cenoura).
The plan step stored other spellings (ancora, helicoptero, cactus, igloo) as accepted alternates.
Swapped by a reviewer: the kept cacto picture was green in a line-style set, so the line drawing was used instead.

languages.name: Hindi
languages.summary: Picture sets work; automatic spoken scoring isn't reliable yet (10-14/20).

recommended.answer_form: a frame (यह बिल्ली है) was tried and didn't help; use the bare word

notes: Picture set, two items to review: हार्प (harp) was named वीणा (veena, an Indian instrument). The harp is unfamiliar in India; replace the item.
Picture set: सीटी (whistle) drawings were read as a microphone or an ektara.
Also named: one cactus picture as नागफनी (the native name for prickly pear), and one kettle picture as चायदानी (teapot).
The transcriber sometimes switches script. It wrote loanwords in Latin letters ('cactus', 'Kaitly'; accepted as alternates now) and इग्लू in Bengali (এগুলো).
Fixed: the tokenizer split Hindi words at vowel signs (बिल्ली -> ब ल ल), so no Hindi response could score Correct before Oct 26.
Only one Hindi macOS voice (Lekha); two identical runs gave 13 and 10 (14 and 11 with alternates).

languages.name: Mandarin Chinese
languages.summary: Works when people name with a measure word (18/20 and 17/20). There are no sound-based error codes (Formal, Mixed, Nonword) for Chinese.

recommended.answer_form: with a measure word (一只猫, 一把剪刀)

notes: Bare one-syllable names come back as homophones: 锚 -> 毛 (both máo), 锯子 -> 句子, 竖琴 -> 树禽. Telling them apart needs pinyin, which we don't have offline.
Picture set, two items to review: both 水壶 (kettle) pictures looked like teapots and were named 茶壶; and 手套 was planned as a pair of gloves, so SAM saw two objects.
The plan prompt now asks for exactly one object and no colors. A retry kept a single glove, but 水壶 still drew as a teapot.
Swapped by a reviewer: the kept 胡萝卜 (carrot) picture was orange in a line-style set, so the line drawing was used instead.
Muse Spark named one umbrella picture 伞 instead of 雨伞; it is a good alternate to accept in review.
Fixed: Chinese scoring crashed without the jieba package. It now splits words itself, removes measure words, and maps traditional characters to simplified.
